title: A Different Angle on Paintings
transcript: A small gallery borrowed several landscape paintings whose glossy surfaces reflected the ceiling lights. Visitors often stepped sideways to see past the bright patches. The curator kept the bulbs at the same brightness and tested two ways of aiming them. She switched between the settings at lunchtime and reversed their order on alternate days. An assistant counted how often visitors moved sideways while looking at the paintings. With the lamps aimed more steeply downward, those movements became less frequent. The new angle did create a shadow over the lower edge of one painting, so the curator adjusted that lamp individually before adopting the setting across the room.

questions.prompt: Why did the curator reverse the order of the settings on alternate days?
options: To give the bulbs time to cool down.
To let visitors compare both settings in one visit.
To reduce the influence of the time of day on the comparison.
To match the brightness of the lamps to the weather.
questions.answer: To reduce the influence of the time of day on the comparison.
questions.explanation: 每天中午切换灯光，并隔天颠倒顺序，使两种设置都能在上午和下午接受观察。

questions.prompt: What happened when the lamps were aimed more steeply downward?
options: Visitors stood closer to the frames.
Visitors spent less time in the room.
Visitors moved more quickly between paintings.
questions.explanation: 灯光以更陡的角度向下照射时，访客侧移的次数减少了。
